speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn experiencing feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To help me diagnose the cause, how many days old are you, and is this vomiting projectile or continuous?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus.

Given the patient is only six hours old, presenting with bilious vomiting and intolerance since birth, this is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. Pyloric stenosis is unlikely as it typically presents at 3-6 weeks of age. Please confirm if there are any abdominal distension or signs of peritonitis, but immediate surgical consultation is required.
